text:
Alejandro: heads-up — saw a customer hit a bunch of 429s last night but their org-level usage looked fine. looks like per-key burst tokens were exhausted while org pool still had spare capacity.
Mira: interesting — were the 429s coming from sustained load or bursts?
Alejandro: short bursts, lots of concurrent small requests from one api-key. per-key token-bucket (100/s burst, refill 10/s) kicked in, so requests hit immediate 429. org-level queueing didn't help because we short-circuit at per-key check.
Jamal: that's expected behavior today. per-key limits are enforced before queueing to avoid noisy-key hogs.
Priya: question: should we instead let per-key overflow into an org-level queue for short bursts? could avoid 429s and keep requests warm, but risk head-of-line blocking.
Mira: tradeoff: letting overflow means a spike from one key can raise org latency for everyone. but strict cutoffs are surprising to customers.
Alejandro: customer feedback is "why do I get 429 while my org still has capacity?" — UX problem.
Jamal: maybe we can do tiered behavior: for paid orgs with SLAs, allow per-key burst borrowing with a short leash (max queue time 250ms) and preemption for higher-priority keys. free orgs keep strict 429s.
Priya: love that. Implementation notes: adjust order — check org budget first, then per-key. If per-key exhausted but org budget available and key tier allows, enqueue with priority score = key_weight / request_cost.
Mira: need clear observability: dashboard panels for per-key queue depth, avg wait time, and rejected-by-reason (per-key-limit vs org-capacity). otherwise we'll be blind.
Jamal: agree. also add a new response hint so clients know why a request was dropped. propose adding headers: `X-Quota-Reason: per_key_limit|org_limit|queue_full` and `Retry-After` where applicable.
Alejandro: +1. also want a small change in body for SDKs: `quota_status` in JSON with `{"reason":"per_key_limit","tokens_remaining":0}` so SDKs can surface friendly messages.
Priya: on HTTP codes: should we map queue-full to 503 instead of 429? semantics: 429 = rate limit on caller; 503 = service overloaded. If we choose 503 for queue-full, some clients will retry with exponential backoff which we probably want for service overload. But 503 could trigger client-side circuit breakers.
Mira: i'd prefer 429 for per-key limits and 503 for system-level shedding (e.g., when global queue > threshold). queue overflow due to permissive per-key borrowing -> ambiguous.
Jamal: proposal: error code mapping: per-key hard limit -> 429, org quota exhausted -> 429, queue timeout or service overload -> 503. For per-key borrowing rejection (we allowed enqueue but queue full) -> 503 with `X-Quota-Reason: queue_full`.
Alejandro: sounds reasonable. Also add metric labels: `reject_reason` tag for all rejects, so dashboards can split 429 vs 503 and correlate with org tiers.
Priya: rollout plan: feature-flag the per-key borrowing and new headers. 1) enable for internal orgs only, 2) canary 5% of paid orgs, 3) ramp with alert on per-org latency > 20th percentile.
deploy-bot: flag `per_key_borrowing` toggled ON for group "internal-canary" at 2026-03-18T14:12:03Z
Mira: need acceptance tests: 1) high-concurrency single-key spike should not starve other keys in same org; 2) header/populated `quota_status` for both success and error responses; 3) metric emitted `queue_wait_ms` and `reject_reason`.
Jamal: implementation detail: use moving-window histograms for queue_wait_ms and expose p50/p95 on console. Also track `tokens_borrowed` per key.
Alejandro: question on storage: per-key state currently in redis with 100ms TTL churn. if we allow borrowing we need accurate queue depth — prefer an in-memory token-capped queue on the router node with eventual persistence to redis for accounting.
Priya: agree. want a fallback path: if router node memory full, immediately return 503 and increment `reject_reason=router_mem_limit`.
Mira: telemetry hooks: add trace spans around "quota.check" "enqueue" "dequeue" so we can tie latency regressions to quota/queue.
Alejandro: can someone draft the API change for headers + quota_status schema? I'll correlate with SDKs.
Priya: I'll write the RFC and include examples for Go/python SDK.
Jamal: i'll prototype router-side queue and preemption logic this week. ping me if you want to pair.
Alejandro: thanks — seems we're aligned. small follow-up: can we show per-key queue usage in the Console next to the key settings page? customers ask for that.
Mira: yep, add a small sparkline + current queue length + last reject reason.
deploy-bot: experiment `per_key_borrowing` staged to 5% paid orgs at 2026-03-18T14:28:25Z
rate-limiter-bot: alert muted: per_key_borrowing-canary spikes observed, created ticket #PLT-4387
Jamal: noted ticket. i'll check logs and push a fix if preemption logic misorders.
Alejandro: :thumbsup: good progress. we'll sync at the eng-platform sync tomorrow to approve rollout timeline.
